thread_analysis.thread_summary: Ricoh Imaging camera (R0910) report review thread covering a passed Bluetooth profile test. The internal report reviewer (Tanaka) flagged minor report formatting issues (date format, duplicate filename) and reminded the tester to check for a newer PTS version before testing. When the tester (Ushiroebisu) tried updating to the newly-released PTS 8.9.1, it produced an unprecedented error message never seen before, so the tester reverted to the stable 8.8.1 to run the test. Sakai used this to reaffirm Allion's standing internal guidance: avoid the very latest PTS version, especially fresh '.0' builds released just days earlier, since new releases can introduce tool-side bugs or stability issues.
all_questions_found: Should we use the latest PTS version for our profile test, or is an older version safer?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: PTS versions have a history of introducing regressions where stability or tool behavior changes unexpectedly right after release. In this case, the tester updated to PTS 8.9.1 (released just 3 days earlier, June 7, 2025) and encountered an error message never seen in prior testing, so reverted to the previously-validated 8.8.1 version to complete the test. Sakai's internal guidance is to always avoid brand-new PTS releases, especially fresh '.0' builds, since new versions have historically caused bugs, dongle/licensing constraints, or unexpected behavior (such as an unnecessary Viewer check appearing) that block or disrupt testing - not necessarily DUT failures.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: PTS version selection is a risk management decision. The risk is asymmetric: using an older stable version is very low risk (SIG accepts it), while using the very latest version carries the risk of tool bugs causing false failures and timeline delays. Always select PTS version based on lab-confirmed stability, not recency.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using a brand-new, unvalidated PTS version risks encountering tool bugs, licensing/dongle constraints, or unexpected behavior that blocks or disrupts a scheduled test session, causing avoidable delays. A reviewer with more recent hands-on PTS experience (e.g., Ushiroebisu) may catch instability that a reviewer who tested in an earlier, more stable period (e.g., Tanaka) does not anticipate.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified. Sakai proactively reiterated the standing internal guidance to avoid the very latest PTS release, and the tester appropriately reverted to a known-stable version rather than troubleshooting the new version's error under time pressure.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always avoid the very latest PTS release, especially a build still in its first few days post-launch (fresh '.0' or minor releases) - prefer a version with a track record of successful use at the lab. When report reviewers disagree on whether 'the latest version has bugs' is still true, defer to the most recent hands-on testing experience, not to assumptions formed during an earlier, more stable period.
